about: The Internet Security POV policy. Every rule gets the POV prefix, the POV rule label and the zpov:<pov-id> stamp, and applies only to the customer's pilot group. Categories, file types, DLP engines, isolation profiles and Cloud App Control actions are checked against the tenant during discovery; anything the tenant lacks is left out with a note in the change list. Names stay within ZIA's 31 characters including the prefix. Starting values come from the AI Guard SE Demo Kit's ZIA template (checked against a live tenant, Oct 2026).

url_category.name: tenant check
url_category.description: Blocked only for the POV pilot group. If the probe sees this blocked, the device is in the customer's tenant.

network_service.name: POV ports
network_service.description: Unusual ports the POV probe tries.

url_filtering.name: Block DNS over HTTPS
url_filtering.why: Stops lookups that hide from DNS control by going over HTTPS (browsers fall back to ordinary DNS).

ssl_inspection.name: Bypass finance and health
ssl_inspection.why: Listed first so it sits above the inspect rule.

ssl_inspection.name: Inspect pilot group
ssl_inspection.why: EICAR over HTTPS, DLP, file type control and Cloud App Control only work on decrypted traffic.

sandbox.name: Sandbox never-seen files
sandbox.why: Holds files no one has seen before (PDF, Office, executables, ZIP) while Cloud Sandbox analyses them; blocks what it finds malicious.

firewall.name: Block POV ports
firewall.why: Firewall and DNS rules see traffic only from devices on Z-Tunnel 2.0 (the Client Connector module sets that).

dns.name: Block marijuana DNS
dns.why: A category the web tests don't visit, so DNS blocks never hide the URL filtering results.

customer_actions.name: Malware Protection blocks viruses and unwanted apps
customer_actions.why: Malware and Advanced Threat Protection are tenant-wide policies the customer owns, so the kit never changes them.
